INDUSTRIAL LEASE AGREEMENT

THIS INDUSTRIAL LEASE AGREEMENT (this "Lease") is entered into effective as of the 1st day of February, 2021 (the "Effective Date"), by and between COYOTE CREEK BUSINESS PARK OWNER LLC, a California limited liability company ("Landlord"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL GROUP, INC., a Delaware corporation d/b/a Meridian Plumbing, Heating & Air, with a principal place of business at 2150 Harbor Point Drive, Suite 400, Sacramento, California 95833 ("Tenant").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Landlord is the owner of certain real property commonly known as 1890 Lundy Avenue, San Jose, California, and more particularly described in the legal description attached hereto as Exhibit A (the "Land"); and

WHEREAS, Landlord desires to lease to Tenant, and Tenant desires to lease from Landlord, a portion of the Land consisting of approximately 11,800 rentable square feet (the "Premises"), upon the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Landlord and Tenant agree as follows:

1. PREMISES

1.1 Lease of Premises. Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises, which constitutes a portion of the building located at 1890 Lundy Avenue, San Jose, California, consisting of approximately 11,800 rentable square feet, including industrial warehouse space and associated office areas, loading dock facilities, and parking areas as shown on the floor plan attached hereto as Exhibit B (the "Floor Plan"). The Premises shall be referred to herein collectively as the "Premises."

1.2 Condition of Premises. Tenant acknowledges that it has inspected the Premises and accepts the Premises in their "as-is" condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted. Landlord makes no warranty as to the suitability of the Premises for Tenant's particular use or business. Tenant shall be responsible for all alterations, improvements, and repairs necessary to make the Premises suitable for Tenant's operations, subject to Landlord's prior written consent as set forth in Section 8 hereof.

1.3 Common Areas. Tenant shall have the right to use, in common with Landlord and other tenants occupying space in the building, the common areas and facilities, including parking areas, access roads, utility areas, and loading facilities, which rights of use shall be exercised in accordance with Landlord's reasonable rules and regulations from time to time established.

2. TERM

2.1 Lease Term. The initial term of this Lease (the "Initial Term") shall commence on the 1st day of February, 2021 (the "Commencement Date") and shall terminate at 11:59 p.m. on the 31st day of January, 2026, unless sooner terminated in accordance with the provisions hereof. Time is of the essence in this Lease.

2.2 Renewal Option. Tenant shall have one (1) option (the "Renewal Option") to renew this Lease for an additional term of three (3) years (the "Renewal Term"), upon the same terms and conditions as are contained herein, except that the Base Rent during the Renewal Term shall be adjusted as set forth in Section 2.3, provided that:

(a) Tenant is not in material default under this Lease beyond any applicable cure period as of the date of exercise of this option or as of the commencement of the Renewal Term;

(b) Tenant or an affiliate of Tenant occupies at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the Premises as of the date of exercise and as of the commencement of the Renewal Term; and

(c) Tenant shall exercise this Renewal Option, if at all, by delivering written notice to Landlord not less than one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the Initial Term.

2.3 Renewal Option Exercise. Tenant has exercised its Renewal Option by written notice delivered to Landlord on October 30, 2025. The Renewal Term shall commence on February 1, 2026 and shall terminate at 11:59 p.m. on January 31, 2029. The Base Rent for the Renewal Term shall be equal to Ninety-Five Percent (95%) of the average fair market rental rate per rentable square foot for comparable industrial properties in the San Jose, California market area, as of February 1, 2026, as mutually agreed upon by Landlord and Tenant or, if the parties cannot agree, as determined by independent appraisers selected in accordance with Section 2.4 below.

2.4 Fair Market Rent Determination. If Landlord and Tenant cannot agree upon the fair market rental rate for the Renewal Term on or before one hundred (100) days prior to the commencement of the Renewal Term, either party may submit the matter to appraisal. Each party shall select one independent appraiser with at least ten (10) years of experience in appraising industrial properties in the San Jose area. The two appraisers shall select a third appraiser within ten (10) days. The Base Rent shall be established as the average of the two appraisals that are closest in value. The costs of the appraisers shall be shared equally by Landlord and Tenant.

2.5 Holdover. If Tenant remains in occupancy of the Premises after the expiration of the Lease Term (including any Renewal Term) without execution of a new lease or written agreement for extended occupancy, Tenant shall be deemed a tenant at sufferance, and Landlord shall have the right to recover possession without notice or demand, and Tenant shall pay rent at the rate of one hundred twenty-five percent (125%) of the Base Rent in effect immediately prior to the expiration date, payable monthly in advance until Tenant vacates.

3. RENT AND ADDITIONAL CHARGES

3.1 Base Rent. Commencing on the Commencement Date and continuing throughout the Initial Term, Tenant shall pay to Landlord, without demand, deduction, or offset (except as expressly provided herein), annual Base Rent in the amount of Two Hundred Ninety Thousand Two Hundred Eighty Dollars ($290,280.00), payable in equal monthly installments of Twenty-Four Thousand One Hundred Ninety Dollars ($24,190.00), in advance, on the first day of each calendar month during the Lease Term. The Base Rent is calculated at the rate of Two Dollars and Five Cents ($2.05) per rentable square foot per month.

3.2 Payment of Rent. All rental payments shall be made payable to Landlord or to such other party as Landlord shall from time to time designate in writing, and shall be delivered to Landlord at the address specified in Section 15 hereof or to such other address as Landlord may designate in writing. Rent payment shall be made in accordance with Landlord's then-current payment instructions, which may include payment by electronic transfer, check, or other mutually acceptable means.

3.3 Late Charges. If any rent payment is not received by Landlord within five (5) days after the due date, Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount. Tenant shall also pay interest on the overdue amount at the rate of ten percent (10%) per annum (or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less) from the due date until paid. The acceptance of any late payment with a late charge or interest shall not constitute a waiver of any default or breach by Tenant.

3.4 Taxes and Operating Expenses. Tenant shall pay its proportionate share of real property taxes and operating expenses (including common area maintenance, insurance, utilities for common areas, and other reasonable operating costs) attributable to the building and common areas. Landlord shall provide Tenant with an annual estimate of such charges on or before December 31 of each year, and Tenant shall pay monthly installments equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual amount. Within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall provide an accounting of actual costs, and if actual costs exceed estimated costs, Tenant shall pay the difference within thirty (30) days. If estimated costs exceed actual costs, Landlord shall credit the overage against future rent payments.

3.5 Parking and Common Area Maintenance. In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay monthly charges for maintenance and management of the parking areas and common facilities in an amount to be specified by Landlord, such charges to be prorated based on Tenant's proportionate share of the building, calculated as 100% because Tenant occupies the entire building.

4. UTILITIES

4.1 Additional Utility Services. Tenant shall be responsible for all utilities consumed by the Premises, including but not limited to electricity, natural gas, water, sewer, and trash collection. If utilities are not separately metered for the Premises, Landlord shall allocate utility costs based on Tenant's proportionate square footage or actual consumption as measured by separate meters to be installed at Tenant's expense if Landlord determines that separate metering is practicable. Tenant shall contract directly with the applicable utility providers for service to the Premises where available. Landlord may enter the Premises at reasonable times upon forty-eight (48) hours' notice to read meters and inspect utility installations.

4.2 Utility Interruption. Landlord shall not be liable for any failure or interruption of utilities due to acts of third parties, including the utility companies, maintenance work, accidents, or force majeure events. Tenant shall maintain backup power systems adequate for Tenant's operations, including backup generators as reasonably necessary for Tenant's HVAC and plumbing operations.

4.3 Exterior Lighting. Landlord shall maintain exterior lighting in the common areas and parking facilities. The cost of such lighting shall be included in the operating expenses charged to Tenant.

5. USE OF PREMISES

5.1 Permitted Use. The Premises shall be used and occupied solely by Tenant for the operation of Tenant's plumbing, heating, and air conditioning contractor business, including administrative offices, equipment storage, vehicle parking, and related commercial operations (the "Permitted Use"), and for no other purpose without the prior written consent of Landlord. Tenant shall not conduct any use that would violate any law, statute, ordinance, or regulation, or that would be objectionable to Landlord or other occupants of the building.

5.2 Hazardous Materials. Tenant shall not place, store, or use any Hazardous Materials (as defined below) in the Premises except in the ordinary course of Tenant's business in reasonable quantities and in compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations. Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord of any spill, release, or suspected contamination involving Hazardous Materials. "Hazardous Materials" means any substance, material, or waste that is regulated as hazardous, toxic, radioactive, or otherwise regulated under any federal, state, or local environmental law, including but not limited to petroleum products, asbestos, mold, and refrigerants used in HVAC systems.

5.3 Nuisance and Disturbance. Tenant shall not create or permit any nuisance, disturbance, or condition that would materially interfere with the use and occupancy of other areas of the building or with the rights of other occupants or neighboring properties. Tenant shall operate its business in a professional manner and shall comply with all noise ordinances.

5.4 Compliance with Laws. Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, ordinances, regulations, and requirements relating to Tenant's use and occupancy of the Premises, including without limitation the Americans with Disabilities Act, environmental protection laws, occupational safety and health standards, and building and fire codes.

6. MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS

6.1 Landlord's Maintenance Obligations. Landlord shall maintain the structural components of the building, including the roof, exterior walls, foundation, and main mechanical systems serving the building, in good condition and repair, ordinary wear and tear excepted. Landlord shall also maintain common areas, parking facilities, and landscaping.

6.2 Tenant's Maintenance Obligations. Tenant shall, at Tenant's sole cost and expense, keep the Premises and all fixtures, equipment, and improvements within the Premises in good order, condition, and state of repair, including but not limited to:

(a) All interior walls, ceilings, and flooring;

(b) All interior doors, locks, and hardware;

(c) All interior glass and windows;

(d) All interior plumbing fixtures and equipment;

(e) All interior electrical outlets and fixtures (excluding the main electrical panel);

(f) All HVAC equipment serving only the Premises;

(g) Loading dock areas and doors;

(h) Interior dock equipment and ramps; and

(i) All other improvements and fixtures installed by or for Tenant.

6.3 Replacements and Repairs. Tenant shall make all necessary repairs promptly when needed. Landlord shall have the right, but not the obligation, to make any repairs that Tenant fails to make within ten (10) days after written notice from Landlord (or immediately in case of emergency), and Tenant shall reimburse Landlord within thirty (30) days for all costs incurred, plus interest at ten percent (10%) per annum.

6.4 Maintenance of Grounds. Tenant shall maintain the grounds surrounding the Premises in a neat and clean condition, including removal of debris, maintenance of landscaping if applicable, and removal of snow and ice in compliance with local ordinances.

7. INSURANCE

7.1 Tenant's Insurance. Throughout the Lease Term and any Renewal Term, Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, maintain the following insurance coverage:

(a) Commercial General Liability insurance with limits of not less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) per occurrence and Four Million Dollars ($4,000,000) aggregate, covering bodily injury, property damage, and personal injury;

(b) Property insurance covering all property, fixtures, equipment, and improvements of Tenant within the Premises at their full replacement value;

(c) Workers' Compensation insurance as required by the State of California;

(d) Business Automobile Liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence; and

(e) Employers Liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence.

7.2 Insurance Requirements. All insurance policies required hereunder shall:

(a) Be issued by insurers rated A- or better by A.M. Best and authorized to do business in the State of California;

(b) Provide that coverage shall not be cancelled, materially altered, or allowed to lapse without at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Landlord;

(c) Name Landlord and its lenders as additional insureds on the commercial general liability and auto liability policies;

(d) Be primary insurance, with any insurance carried by Landlord being excess and non-contributing; and

(e) Include waiver of subrogation in favor of Landlord.

7.3 Certificate of Insurance. Tenant shall provide Landlord with certificates of insurance evidencing compliance with these requirements on or before the Commencement Date and annually thereafter on or before the anniversary of the Commencement Date. If Tenant fails to provide evidence of required insurance, Landlord may obtain such insurance at Tenant's expense.

7.4 Landlord's Insurance. Landlord shall maintain fire and extended coverage insurance on the building structure at Landlord's cost, which cost shall be included in the operating expenses charged to Tenant.

8. ALTERATIONS

8.1 Alterations Requiring Consent. Tenant shall not make any structural alterations, modifications, or improvements to the Premises or any part thereof (collectively, "Alterations") without first obtaining the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Non-structural alterations of a routine nature that do not affect the structural integrity, roof, exterior, or main building systems, and that cost less than Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000) per instance, shall not require Landlord's consent, provided that Tenant notifies Landlord and complies with the procedural requirements hereof.

8.2 Alterations for Tenant's Operations. Landlord acknowledges that Tenant has advised that it will need to make certain Alterations regarding venting systems for HVAC operations that will require roof penetrations, widening of dock doors, ventilation for storage areas, securing racking to floor slabs, warehouse lighting upgrades, electrical upgrades for equipment, installation of backup generators, and buildout and remodeling of office space, and Landlord's consent to such Alterations shall not be unreasonably withheld.

8.3 Alteration Procedures. Before commencing any Alterations requiring Landlord's consent:

(a) Tenant shall submit detailed plans and specifications to Landlord, prepared by a licensed architect or engineer, for Landlord's written approval, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed;

(b) Tenant shall furnish Landlord with a certified estimate of the cost of the proposed work;

(c) Tenant shall submit for approval to Landlord copies of all proposed contracts and the qualifications of all contractors;

(d) Tenant shall maintain comprehensive general liability insurance on all alteration work;

(e) All work shall be performed in a good and workmanlike manner in full compliance with all applicable laws, building codes, and regulations;

(f) Tenant shall obtain all necessary permits and licenses; and

(g) Tenant shall provide Landlord with evidence of payment to all contractors upon completion.

8.4 Tenant's Mechanics Lien Waiver. Upon completion of any Alterations, Tenant shall provide Landlord with a full and final mechanics lien waiver from Tenant and all contractors and suppliers.

8.5 Removal of Alterations. Upon expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall remove all non-permanent Alterations and restore the Premises to their original condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted, within thirty (30) days after the expiration date, at Tenant's sole cost and expense. Permanent improvements and fixtures shall become the property of Landlord unless Landlord otherwise directs.

9. INDEMNIFICATION

9.1 Tenant's Indemnity. Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord and its officers, employees, and agents from and against all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from or related to:

(a) Tenant's use, occupancy, or conduct in the Premises;

(b) Any injury to persons or damage to property occurring in or about the Premises, unless solely caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Landlord or Landlord's agents;

(c) Any breach or default by Tenant in the performance of any obligation under this Lease;

(d) Any Hazardous Materials brought onto the Premises by Tenant or its agents; and

(e) Any liens or claims arising from Alterations or improvements made by Tenant.

9.2 Waiver of Subrogation. Tenant hereby waives any and all claims, rights, or remedies against Landlord to the extent covered by insurance required hereunder or by any insurance maintained by Tenant.

10. DEFAULT AND REMEDIES

10.1 Events of Default. Tenant shall be in default under this Lease if:

(a) Tenant fails to pay any rent or other charges due under this Lease when due, and such failure continues for five (5) days after written notice;

(b) Tenant abandons the Premises or vacates a substantial portion of the Premises;

(c) Tenant fails to comply with any other term, condition, or covenant of this Lease, and such failure continues for thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord (or such additional time as may be reasonably necessary if the breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days and Tenant diligently pursues a cure);

(d) Tenant becomes insolvent, makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy, is adjudicated a bankrupt, or is liquidated;

(e) A lien or levy is placed against Tenant's personal property or business, and Tenant fails to satisfy or bond the same within ten (10) days; or

(f) Tenant sublets all or substantially all of the Premises without Landlord's consent.

10.2 Landlord's Remedies. Upon any default by Tenant that continues beyond the applicable notice and cure period, Landlord shall have the following remedies:

(a) Landlord may terminate this Lease by delivering written notice of termination to Tenant;

(b) Landlord may re-enter the Premises and remove Tenant's property (or store such property at Tenant's expense), and Landlord may either try to re-lease the Premises or leave it vacant;

(c) Landlord may pursue any other remedy available at law or in equity;

(d) Landlord shall be entitled to recover all costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees and court costs, incurred in enforcing Landlord's rights hereunder or in curing any default by Tenant; and

(e) Tenant shall remain liable for all rent through the remainder of the Lease Term, plus any deficiency between the rent due and the amount recovered from any re-letting.

10.3 Remedies Not Exclusive. No remedy provided herein shall be exclusive or waive Landlord's right to pursue any other remedy available by law or equity.

10.4 Late Rent Not Waived. The acceptance of late rent shall not constitute a waiver of any default or right to enforce any provision of this Lease.

11. REPAIRS AND RESTORATION

11.1 Casualty Damage. If the Premises are damaged or destroyed by fire, earthquake, or other casualty, Landlord shall promptly notify the insurance carriers and shall use the insurance proceeds to repair the Premises, except as provided below.

11.2 Uninsurable Casualty. If the damage is such that it is economically impracticable to repair the Premises (as reasonably determined by Landlord), or if the damage occurs within the last two (2) years of the Lease Term, Landlord may terminate this Lease by written notice given within thirty (30) days of the casualty, in which event this Lease shall terminate and Tenant shall vacate within sixty (60) days.

11.3 Repair by Landlord. If Landlord elects to repair, Landlord shall do so with reasonable diligence, using insurance proceeds. During the period of repair, rent shall abate proportionately to the extent Tenant is unable to use the Premises.

11.4 Restoration by Tenant. Tenant shall be responsible for restoration of all Tenant's property, fixtures, equipment, and non-permanent improvements. Tenant's insurance proceeds shall be used for such restoration.

12. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING

12.1 Restriction on Transfer. Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet any part of the Premises without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Any attempted assignment without consent shall be void. The terms "assign" and "assignment" include any transfer, whether voluntary or involuntary, by operation of law or otherwise.

12.2 Conditions to Consent. As a condition to Landlord's consent to any assignment or sublease, Tenant shall:

(a) Provide Landlord with detailed financial statements of the proposed assignee or subtenant;

(b) Enter into a written agreement whereby the assignee or subtenant assumes in writing all obligations under this Lease;

(c) Provide Landlord with evidence that the assignee or subtenant has sufficient financial capability to perform all obligations hereunder; and

(d) If there is a profit from the sublease or assignment, pay to Landlord fifty percent (50%) of such profit.

12.3 No Release of Tenant. No assignment or subletting shall relieve Tenant of any obligation hereunder. Tenant shall remain primarily liable for all rent and other obligations throughout the Lease Term.

13. NOTICES

13.1 Methods of Notice. Any notice required or permitted under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed given when personally delivered, sent by certified mail (return receipt requested), sent by overnight courier service (FedEx, UPS, or similar), or sent by email with confirmation of receipt. Notices shall be addressed as follows:

TO LANDLORD:

Coyote Creek Business Park Owner LLC
c/o Property Management

San Jose, California

14. GENERAL PROVISIONS

14.1 Entire Agreement. This Lease, including all exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between Landlord and Tenant concerning the Premises and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements. No modification or amendment shall be valid unless in writing and signed by both parties.

14.2 Severability. If any provision of this Lease is held invalid or unenforceable, all other provisions shall remain in full force and effect, and the invalid provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable.

14.3 Governing Law. This Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Venue shall be in the courts located in Santa Clara County, California.

14.4 Waiver. Waiver of any breach shall not constitute waiver of any subsequent breach or of any other provision. Failure to enforce any right shall not constitute waiver of such right.

14.5 Binding Effect. This Lease shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and assigns.

14.6 Authority. Each party represents and warrants that it has full power and authority to enter into this Lease and that the person executing this Lease on its behalf is duly authorized to do so.

14.7 Quiet Enjoyment. Landlord shall provide Tenant with quiet enjoyment of the Premises during the Lease Term, subject to the terms and conditions hereof.

14.8 Surrender of Premises. Upon expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall surrender the Premises in clean condition, with all Alterations removed and the Premises restored to their original condition (reasonable wear and tear excepted), and Tenant shall remove all of Tenant's personal property. If Tenant fails to surrender the Premises, Landlord shall have the right to remove all personal property and store it at Tenant's expense, or to dispose of it at Tenant's expense.

14.9 Right of Entry. Landlord shall have the right to enter the Premises at reasonable times upon forty-eight (48) hours' notice (except in emergencies requiring immediate entry) to inspect the Premises, make repairs or alterations, show the Premises to prospective tenants or lenders during the last six (6) months of the Lease Term, and exercise any other rights under this Lease.

14.10 Broker Representation. Tenant represents and warrants that Tenant has not dealt with any real estate broker, agent, or other intermediary in connection with this Lease. If any broker claims a commission as a result of Tenant's actions, Tenant shall indemnify Landlord for any such claim.

14.11 Environmental Compliance. Tenant shall comply with all applicable environmental laws and regulations and shall promptly notify Landlord of any environmental contamination, release, or threatened release of Hazardous Materials at the Premises. Upon termination of this Lease, Tenant shall remove all Hazardous Materials brought onto the Premises by Tenant and shall restore the Premises to their pre-contaminated condition.

14.12 Subordination. Tenant's rights under this Lease shall be subordinate to any mortgage or deed of trust which may be placed on the property by Landlord, provided that any mortgagee or beneficiary shall agree to subordination for the benefit of Tenant's interest herein upon request.

14.13 Relationship of Parties. Nothing in this Lease shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture, or agency relationship between Landlord and Tenant.

14.14 Cumulative Remedies. The remedies provided herein are cumulative and not exclusive.

15. TERM SUMMARY

The following is a summary of key commercial terms for reference:

Tenant: Meridian Mechanical Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation d/b/a Meridian Plumbing, Heating & Air

Commencement Date: February 1, 2021
Initial Term Expiration: January 31, 2026
Renewal Option: Three (3) years (exercised October 30, 2025)
Renewal Term: February 1, 2026 through January 31, 2029
Base Rent (Initial Term): $2.05 per square foot per month ($24,190.00 monthly)
Base Rent (Renewal Term): To be determined per Section 2.3 and 2.4
Utilities: Tenant responsibility (see Section 4)
Use: Plumbing, heating, and air conditioning contractor business
Permitted Alterations: As described in Section 8.2
